title: API security: is every request authorized for the exact object it touches?
short: Check the caller's right to each object in code on every request, and replay every call with a second tenant's token before each release.
answer: Check in code, on every request, that the caller may act on the exact object and fields it names, and add tests this month that replay each endpoint with a second tenant's token. Use the gateway for token checks, rate limits, schema checks and the version inventory, and switch off any API that isn't in that inventory.
audience: Developers, architects and platform teams that build web, mobile or partner APIs (REST, GraphQL, gRPC, webhooks), and the security staff who review them

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Authorize every object in the handler.
items.text: Look up records by tenant and ID together. OWASP calls broken object level authorization extremely common[^owaspapi1]. In July 2026 CISA listed as exploited a Langflow flaw that let users run other users' flows by ID[^kev].

items.title: Accept and return only allowlisted fields.
items.text: Bind each request to an input schema per endpoint, and build responses from an explicit output type, not a generic `to_json()` of the database object[^owaspapi3].

items.title: Validate every token fully at the API.
items.text: Check signature, algorithm, issuer, audience, expiry and scope[^asvs]. In 2026 attackers exploited SimpleHelp skipping OIDC signature checks and JFrog Artifactory ignoring token scope[^kev].

items.title: Inventory every API and switch off the rest.
items.text: List each host, version and owner, including beta and partner hosts, and block retired versions. The NCSC traces the Optus breach to a forgotten API that stayed online for years[^ncscblog].

items.title: Test with a second tenant before each release.
items.text: Replay every call with another tenant's token, a lower role and no token, and block the release on any success[^owaspapi1].

blocks.title: Test an API for authorization flaws

items.title: Set up two tenants.
items.text: Give each an admin, a basic user and one object of every type. CISA advises testing with users of different privilege levels[^aa23208a].

items.title: Collect every call.
items.text: Take them from the spec, the gateway and recorded web and mobile traffic, including old versions and GraphQL operations.

items.title: Swap the caller.
items.text: Send each request with the other tenant's token, the basic user's token and no token. Expect 401, 403 or 404.

items.title: Swap the IDs and fields.
items.text: Change IDs in paths, bodies and batches. Add `role`, `tenantId` or `isAdmin` to writes and check they are ignored.

items.title: Keep each case as a CI test.
items.text: Run them for every route. NIST suggests deploying an endpoint only once it carries a permission annotation[^nist228].

blocks.title: How API attacks work now
items: **Logged-in users reach other users' data.** In OWASP's 2025 Top 10 data, 100% of applications tested had some form of broken access control, a category that also covers SSRF and CSRF[^owasptop10]. Three of the API Top 10's first five risks are about authorization[^nist228].

**Old and side-door endpoints let attackers in.** OWASP says unmanaged APIs are usually breached via old versions or unpatched endpoints[^owaspapi9]. The NCSC says weak authentication and no rate limiting in Dell's partner portal API exposed details of 49 million customers[^ncscblog].

blocks.title: Tokens and sign-in
items: **Use the code flow with PKCE.** RFC 9700 forbids the password grant, advises against the implicit grant and requires PKCE for public clients[^rfc9700].
**Bind each token to one API.** Restrict access tokens to one audience and the least privilege; an API must refuse tokens meant for another[^rfc9700]. Identify users by `iss` plus `sub`[^asvs].

**Sender-constrain tokens, high-value ones first.** RFC 9700 recommends mutual TLS or DPoP for all access tokens, and requires sender-constrained or rotated refresh tokens for public clients[^rfc9700].

**Keep lifetimes short.** Authorization codes last at most 10 minutes and refresh tokens need an absolute expiry[^asvs]. Keep access tokens to minutes. Give outside callers opaque tokens, not JWTs that reveal internal claims[^nist228].

**Don't rely on API keys alone.** The NCSC calls them shared bearer tokens, often broad and without expiry[^ncscauth]. Authenticate partner and service clients with `private_key_jwt` or mutual TLS[^rfc9700].

blocks.title: Gateway or code: what goes where
items: **The gateway checks who and how much.** Validate tokens, reject requests outside the schema, cap payload size and time, and log every call[^nist228][^ncscexposure].
**The code checks which object.** Ownership, tenant, record state and field rules need the data, so the service decides, or a policy service it asks.

**Make the gateway impossible to skip.** Accept traffic only from the gateway, by network policy or a credential it attaches[^nist228]. In January 2026 CISA listed a Versa Concerto proxy flaw that exposed admin endpoints[^kev].
**Strip identity headers at the edge.** Clients must not be able to set headers such as `X-User-ID` that the gateway sets[^asvs].
**Rate-limit per caller.** Key limits to the user or credential over 1 to 5 minutes and cap concurrent requests; a total limit lets one caller crowd out the rest[^nist228].

blocks.title: Webhooks, GraphQL and gRPC
items: **Verify every webhook you receive.** Check the HMAC over the raw body in constant time[^ghwebhook][^stripe], reject old timestamps (Stripe's libraries allow 5 minutes by default) and skip event IDs already processed[^stripe].

**Treat webhook URLs you call as hostile.** CISA listed a GitLab webhook SSRF as exploited in February 2026[^kev]. Allowlist hosts, check the address you connect to and refuse redirects, as the TypeScript sheet explains.
**Cap GraphQL query cost.** Use depth and amount limits or cost analysis[^asvs], limit batching and check authorization on both edges and nodes[^owaspgql].

**Hide the schema on public endpoints.** Turn off introspection unless outside parties use the API[^asvs], and GraphiQL in production[^owaspgql]. gRPC's docs flag the reflection service as a possible security issue on public APIs[^grpcrefl].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Checking the role but not the record.** NIST counts a missing resource-level check, or one against the wrong user or resource, as an authorization risk[^nist228].
**Letting the app hide fields.** Attackers read the raw API, and decompile mobile apps to find endpoints and keys[^ncscexposure].

**Leaving a beta host behind.** In OWASP's example, a rate limit in front of the production reset API didn't cover a beta host running the same code, where a researcher brute-forced the 6-digit token[^owaspapi9].

**Calling other services with the backend's own token.** Pass the caller on by token exchange and base each decision on their permissions[^asvs], or one bug in the first service reaches every service behind it.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Browser apps should keep tokens on a backend.** RFC 10017, a Best Current Practice since August 2026, strongly recommends a backend for frontend, which keeps tokens out of the browser, for business apps and apps that handle personal data[^rfc10017].

**Agent-facing APIs need the same checks.** MCP's July 2026 specification deprecates Dynamic Client Registration[^mcpchange], and in September CISA listed a LiteLLM MCP endpoint that accepted any bearer token[^kev]. Inventory and test MCP servers like any other API.
**NIST's API guidance gained checklists.** The March 2026 update of SP 800-228 adds tables of API risks and of controls by lifecycle stage[^nist228].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Waiting for OAuth 2.1.** It is still a draft, at version 17 in October 2026[^oauth21]. RFC 9700 already sets the rules[^rfc9700].
**Random IDs instead of checks.** CISA says UUIDs and GUIDs should not be used for security capabilities[^aa23208a]. Use them, and check access anyway.
**An API security platform before an inventory and tests.** No traffic product knows that order 1042 belongs to tenant B.
**Signing every message.** ASVS asks for per-message signatures only at its highest level, for highly sensitive requests[^asvs].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Write one `canAccess(user, object, action)` check and call it in every handler that takes an ID.
Use a hosted identity provider with the code flow and PKCE.
Put the API behind your cloud's managed gateway with per-key rate limits.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Generate the inventory from specs and gateway routes, with owners and retirement dates.
Run the two-tenant tests in CI, and turn off introspection and reflection by default.
Alert on bursts of 403 and 404 from one caller, a sign of enumeration[^aa23208a].

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Annotate each endpoint with its permission and enforce it at the gateway via a policy service[^nist228].
Require sender-constrained tokens for payment, health and admin APIs[^asvs].
Pen-test each major release with users of different roles in different tenants.
